clue.text: Where to look out for a dog without an awful din?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dog's letters sit around the rest

parts.note: bow-wow is the nursery word for a dog, from its bark

indicators.note: an awful din is a mess, so its three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to keep watch for a dog that isn't making a dreadful racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'awful' gives INDO. The dog looks like the thing being watched for, but its bark-name is the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved window jutting from a wall is a place for gazing out at the street.

clue.text: Setter and the other man got up and the pair went outside to see a big animal

indicators.note: went outside means this word wraps around the rest

parts.note: the pair, both of them, is both

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the words read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
the other man is simply he

explanation.surface: The setter and another man stood up, and two of them went out to look at a large beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' (upwards in a down clue) gives EHEM, and 'went outside' wraps the pair round it. Gordius, like many setters, calls himself 'Setter'.
explanation.definitionFit: The behemoth is the huge biblical beast of Job, now any enormous creature.

clue.text: Started work with the elderly and got paid for it

indicators.note: started means only the beginning of the word work is used

parts.note: the elderly are the aged

explanation.surface: Someone began a job alongside old people and was paid for doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: Waged describes someone in paid employment, earning a wage for their work.

clue.text: When dealing with minor perils no action is specified

indicators.note: loosely, the letters are set out in a specified new arrangement, signalling a reshuffle

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In facing small dangers, it says no action is laid down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is specified' signals an anagram of PERILS NO ACTION. 'minor' looks like an adjective for the perils, but it is a child in law.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin legal phrase means in the place of a parent, the role a guardian or teacher takes towards a child.

clue.text: Raising a hat to a lady could be a problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat
Emma is a woman's name, any lady

explanation.surface: Doffing your hat to a woman might be awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns LID into DIL, followed by the name EMMA. The surface's raised hat is a polite greeting, a clever cover for the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between two options, a kind of problem.

clue.text: Greeting heard by a spectator?

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: wotcher is a casual Cockney hello, from 'what cheer'

explanation.surface: Is a hello overheard by someone looking on?
explanation.walkthrough: WOTCHER is informal London English for hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is one who looks on, the same as a spectator at an event.

clue.text: He may be among those who speak Urdu

indicators.note: among means the letters are found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man belongs to the Urdu-speaking peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'speaK URDu'. The surface suggests a speaker of Urdu, but Kurds speak Kurdish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kurd is a man of the Kurdish people, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Nude, perhaps without something to put on?

definitions.text: perhaps without something to put on
definitions.meaning: like a salad served with no dressing poured over it

explanation.definitionFit: Undressed means unclothed, and also, of food, served without a dressing.

clue.text: Uninteresting puffs that are found in the woods

definitions.text: that are found in the woods

parts.note: a dry talk is dull, uninteresting
puffs are adverts, ads

explanation.surface: Dull promotional blurbs that turn up out in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryads are tree nymphs of Greek myth, spirits that live in woodland.

clue.text: Tastes in cheese may depend on it

definitions.text: Tastes in cheese may depend on it

indicators.note: the letters' order depends on how they are rearranged, a loose signal to reshuffle

explanation.surface: Whether you like a given cheese could rely on your sense of beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the anagram fodder TASTES IN CHEESE and also the definition: refined taste rests on an aesthetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic sense is the faculty of appreciating beauty and taste, which preferences in cheese rely on.

clue.text: Philosopher, the man rejecting support?

parts.note: the man is he

indicators.note: rejecting means the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: Is this philosopher a man who refuses help?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns LEG into GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was the German idealist thinker known for his dialectic.

clue.text: Modern type of saint was once a presidential candidate

definitions.text: type of saint was once a presidential candidate
definitions.meaning: Mitt Romney, the 2012 Republican candidate, is a Mormon

explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day means of recent times; Mormons call themselves Latter-day Saints.

clue.text: 1960s' teenager — one with Latin (just a little)

parts.note: a mod was a stylish scooter-riding British youth of the 1960s
I is the Roman numeral for one
cum is Latin for with

explanation.surface: A sixties youngster who knows a bit of Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture of sharp suits and scooters.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount, just a little of something.

clue.text: Impetuous type had swallowed almost all other

indicators.note: swallowed means this word takes the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost all means the word other loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A rash person had eaten nearly everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' drops the last letter of 'other'; 'swallowed' makes 'had' the container, though the surface reads it as a greedy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is a rash, quick-tempered person who acts without thinking.

clue.text: Do these make military marches unnecessary?

definitions.text: Do these make military marches unnecessary?

parts.words: Do these make military marches unnecessary?
parts.note: vehicles that carry soldiers spare them from having to march

explanation.surface: Do these vehicles mean soldiers no longer need to march?
explanation.definitionFit: Troop carriers are vehicles or aircraft that transport soldiers, so they need not march.

clue.text: Likely to notice a departed retainer?

parts.note: ob, short for Latin obiit, means died, so departed
a retainer is a household servant

explanation.surface: Would a dead butler be watchful?
explanation.walkthrough: OB, from Latin obiit, is used on gravestones for 'died'.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things, alert.

clue.text: Teacher as censor in coarse upbringing

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other
in a down clue, upbringing means the word is brought up, read bottom to top

parts.note: coarse means rude
Cato the Elder was the famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: A teacher acting as a censor during a rough childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' gives EDUR, and 'in' sets the censor inside. Marcus Porcius Cato held Rome's office of censor, the magistrate overseeing public morals.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is one who teaches, so a teacher.

clue.text: Thinking soberly, dies, is mourned madly

indicators.note: madly means the letters go wild, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone passes away and is grieved over wildly, while others reflect gravely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges DIES IS MOURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious-minded describes a person of earnest, sober thought.

clue.text: Like decimal ruler with greater frequency

parts.note: decimal means of ten, based on tens
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler who likes the decimal system turns up more regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Oftener is an old comparative meaning more often.

clue.text: Seen but perhaps gets hid

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spotted, though maybe it stays out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GETS HID.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted means spotted or seen, as of a ship sighted on the horizon.

clue.text: Ship circling island with diving equipment

indicators.note: circling means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: SS is steamship
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A boat sails round an island carrying gear for divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' makes the ship's two letters the container. SCUBA began as an acronym for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba sets are underwater breathing apparatus used by divers.

clue.text: Nothing in instrument to cover nobility

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument like a small trumpet
O is the zero figure, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in a brass instrument is meant to shelter aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside CORNET: COR-O-NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn on the heads of peers.

clue.text: Regarding the stomach, the state's not quite rigorous

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: not quite means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rigorous means strict

explanation.surface: Concerning digestion, the state's rules are a little lax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims STRICT to STRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach, as in gastric juices.

clue.text: Tory entitlement?

definitions.meaning: a Tory is a member of the political ...
a claim one is due, such as a legal claim

explanation.definitionFit: The Right is the conservative side of politics; a right is also something one is entitled to.

clue.text: With garment girl turns head — it has a hard shell

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment

indicators.note: turns means the word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: Liz is a girl's name
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Wearing underwear, a girl looks round, and she has a hard carapace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes LIZ into ZIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazil nut is a large seed encased in a very tough shell.

clue.text: It's near the time when one should be abed

parts.note: nigh means near

explanation.surface: It's nearly bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness when people sleep.

clue.text: Where to build? It must be in the Home Counties

indicators.note: must be in means this word goes inside the other

parts.note: the Home Counties lie around London in the South East of England, SE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A building plot has to be in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a plot of land where something is built.

clue.text: Day of a left-wing landlord?

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective in the phrase for a special day, so it stands in for 'day' only with that noun

parts.note: red means socialist, left-wing
a letter is one who lets property

explanation.surface: A special occasion for a socialist property owner?
explanation.walkthrough: A red-letter day is a memorable one, from the red ink marking feast days in calendars. A letter here is one who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special, memorable occasion, so the word qualifies that noun.
